description: Snowflake three-valued (NULL) logic on the PREDICATE side: a comparison against NULL is UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN excludes the row exactly as FALSE does - so x <> 'A' drops the NULL row, x = NULL matches nothing, x NOT IN (1, NULL) matches NOTHING at all while x IN (1, NULL) still matches the concrete member, and a NULL join key never finds a partner. The difference between UNKNOWN and FALSE only shows under NOT (NOT of UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN, so the NULL row cannot leak back in) and when the boolean is PROJECTED, where FALSE dominates UNKNOWN under AND and TRUE dominates it under OR. Quantified comparisons follow the same rules: <> ALL over a set containing NULL is the NOT IN twin and is never TRUE, = ANY still matches a concrete member, and a NULL LEFT operand makes the whole comparison UNKNOWN. Ordering is the deliberate opposite of predicate logic - ORDER BY ASC sorts NULLs LAST and DESC sorts them FIRST, with NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST overriding either default, including on the post-GROUP BY sort path. Grouping and set-operation equality (NULL = NULL for GROUP BY, DISTINCT, UNION) is the other deliberate opposite and lives in query-executor-edge-cases. NULLS / LAST / FIRST stay non-reserved. Converted 1:1 from query/NullThreeValuedLogicTest (now retired); row-index reads became whole ordered row sets.

steps.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x <> 'A'
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = NULL
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x NOT IN (1, NULL)
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x IN (1, NULL)
SELECT a.k FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC
SELECT x FROM t WHERE NOT (x < 5)
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x DESC
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC NULLS FIRST
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x DESC NULLS LAST
SELECT x, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY x ORDER BY x ASC NULLS FIRST
SELECT x FROM t WHERE NOT (x = 1 AND 1 = 1)
SELECT x FROM t WHERE NOT (x = 1 OR x = 3)
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x <> ALL (SELECT v FROM s)
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = ANY (SELECT v FROM s)
